title: Noughts & Crosses · Part 2 — Discover iteration
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: In a zero-indexed C# array, which element does array[2] access?
questions.answer: The item at index 2 — the third item.
options: The item at index 1 — the third item.
The item at index 2 — the third item.
The item at index 3 — the third item.
questions.feedback: Model answer: The item at index 2 — the third item.

questions.prompt: Name the three parts of a C# for loop header used to visit every array element.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: A counter, condition and update.

questions.prompt: In a C# 2D array organised as rows and columns, what does GetLength(0) return?
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
questions.feedback: Model answer: The number of rows.

questions.prompt: If a board has 3 rows and 3 columns, how many values does it contain?

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: 2D array — An array with two indexes.
row — A horizontal line of values.
column — A vertical line of values.
dimension — One direction of an array.
nested loop — A loop inside another loop.

blocks.title: Notice the repeated statements
blocks.text: Look at the three explicit row-printing instructions. The operation is the same; only the row index changes: 0, 1, 2 .

blocks.title: Replace the rows with one loop
blocks.text: The first loop repeats the same row-print statement. row changes automatically; each repetition chooses a different row.

blocks.title: Spot the second repetition
blocks.text: Inside each row, we still refer to columns 0, 1 and 2. A second loop can move across the columns of one row.

blocks.title: Put one loop inside the other
blocks.text: Outer loop = down the rows. Inner loop = across the columns. This is called nested iteration .

blocks.title: Worked example · From three statements to one loop, then two
blocks.text: We will improve yesterday's program without changing what it displays. 1 | 2 | 3 4 | 5 | 6 7 | 8 | 9

blocks.title: Write or predict
blocks.text: Study the original three row-print statements. Which part remains identical and which part changes? Console.WriteLine(board[0,0] + " | " + board[0,1] + " | " + board[0,2]); Console.WriteLine(board[1,0] + " | " + board[1,1] + " | " + board[1,2]); Console.WriteLine(board[2,0] + " | " + board[2,1] + " | " + board[2,2]);

blocks.title: What did we discover?
blocks.text: The code prints three values separated by pipes on every row. Only the row index changes (0 → 1 → 2).
